description: Pycoal is a Python library for processing hyperspectral remote-sensing imagery to characterise the impacts of coal and open-pit mining. Its README names AVIRIS and AVIRIS-Next Generation observations, describes the Appalachian mountaintop-mining context and links package documentation. Users provide compatible calibrated spectral imagery and a study boundary; outputs are mapped indicators of mining-related surface materials. Geographic coverage follows the image footprint, with the documented case in the United States. GitHub metadata states GPL-2.0 licensing for the code; remote-sensing input terms are separate. A limitation is that mapped spectral classes require field or independent-image checks and may miss buried or mixed material. The derived land-change layers can support water, road or industrial impact simulations near mines. The QGIS catalogue platform supplies general mapping tools, not this specialised classifier. No AVIRIS imagery or package was downloaded.
name: Pycoal mining-impact image processing
